You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game setup: each token contributed returns 1.2 total split across the group but only 0.3 to the contributor, so keeping tokens is individually dominant even though full contribution maximizes collective payoff. With 10 repeated rounds, this tension between self-interest and group optimum is central to the strategy.

I'll open with a moderately cooperative contribution, maybe 10 out of 20, to signal willingness to cooperate and gauge how others respond before committing further.

Given this tension, I'll aim for a moderate, cooperative-but-cautious approach—contributing something like 10 tokens signals good faith without being fully exploitable, and I can adjust based on how the group responds.
